label: 2D / 3D
gloss: Whether the table is a flat map seen from above (2D), a 3D scene you can turn and tilt (3D), or a flat map with 3D figures or terrain on it, or a switch between both (2D+3D). 3D dice alone don't count here: they have their own column.

label: Runs on
gloss: Where it runs: in a web browser tab, as an installed desktop app (Windows, Mac, Linux), on phones or tablets (iOS, Android), or in a VR headset.

label: Price
gloss: What the game master (GM, who runs the game) pays. free: no paid tier at all. free tier: usable free, with paid upgrades. one-time: a purchase. subscription: a monthly or yearly fee. The note says what players pay.

label: Accounts
gloss: Who must sign up before playing. none: nobody (a link is enough). gm: only the game master. everyone: players too.

label: Fog of war
gloss: Hiding the parts of the map the players have not discovered. yes: built in. partial: manual masks only, or through an add-on.

label: Dynamic lighting
gloss: Light sources and walls that decide what each player's character can see, worked out by the software as tokens move.

label: Map building
gloss: Making maps inside the product (drawing, tiles, a builder or generator), rather than only importing a picture made elsewhere.

label: Levels / height
gloss: Verticality: several floors of a building, stairs, flying or elevation, seen as such rather than as separate flat maps.

label: Sheets & rules
gloss: Character sheets and rules automation: the software knows the game's rules (attacks, damage, conditions) instead of only showing tokens.

label: D&D Beyond / Beyond20
gloss: Rolling from D&D Beyond character sheets into the table, usually through Beyond20 (a free browser extension that sends D&D Beyond rolls to a VTT) or a direct import.

label: Dice
gloss: 3D: physical 3D dice that tumble on screen. roller: a dice roller (text or 2D). no: bring your own.

label: Phones
gloss: Whether a player can take part from a phone. partial: it opens, but some parts do not work or are hard to use.

label: Offline / self-host
gloss: Playing without the maker's servers: offline, on a local network, or on a server you run yourself.

label: Open source
gloss: Whether the source code is published under an open licence (the licence is named in the detail view). partial: some parts only.

label: AI features
gloss: Built-in AI features (generating maps, art or text, an AI assistant at the table). This says only that they exist, not whether that is good.

label: Mods / API
gloss: Add-ons, modules, scripting or a programming interface (API) for extending it.

label: Stage
gloss: How finished the maker says it is.

label: Community signal
gloss: What users visibly say or how big the visible community is, in one line. Not a score.
